summary.text: CA9 is the most convergent candidate: RNA is up in tumour versus normal [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=6.312] and the protein is confirmed [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.269]. It replicates in TCGA-KIRC, survives purity extrapolation and has antibody history (girentuximab, phase 3). It is a diagnostic, imaging and antibody-delivery target, not a functional dependency: DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency and there is no somatic driver mutation.

CD70 is the leading antibody/ADC-type surface candidate after CA9: it is up at protein level [gene=CD70; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.421], replicates in TCGA-KIRC and has clinical-stage antibody and ADC programmes (cusatuzumab, vorsetuzumab mafodotin). Two caveats weaken it: immune cells contribute a large share of its tumour transcripts, so tumour-cell expression cannot be cleanly separated in bulk data, and it was not testable in the confirmatory protein cohort. It is not a DepMap dependency.

Biomarkers and mechanism are separate from targets. NNMT (tumour-up, tumour-intrinsic in both single-cell datasets, protein replicated in the confirmatory cohort, adverse survival) is a prognostic biomarker with no drug and no dependency. PSAT1, ALDH6A1 and PCK1 are down in tumour with protein loss that replicates, and UMOD, ALDOB and SLC22A8 mark loss of proximal-tubule identity. VHL is the disease driver (3p loss), not a differential-expression target. SCARB1 ranks first in the target profile but has a vital-organ (adrenal) proteome signal and an unstable cell-type attribution across the two single-cell datasets, so it is a hypothesis rather than a cleared target.

Several top-ranked signals are negative or microenvironmental. FCER1G and FCGR3A are immune-cell genes whose bulk change follows infiltration; HK2 and PPP1R1A protein changes do not replicate in the confirmatory cohort; and no gene separates the arms of either treatment trial. No candidate shows a selective ccRCC dependency except EPAS1, which has a borderline q-value, so the evidence supports surface-antigen and biomarker uses far better than genetic-vulnerability uses.

Best unexplored candidates, identified and prioritised for experimental validation (not proven). RAB42 is made mostly by RCC cells, replicates in TCGA and is purity-robust, with very few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug; it is an internal protein, not antibody-accessible, and has no selective dependency or survival signal, so a functional knock-down study in ccRCC lines would be the first test. JAG2 is an endothelial Notch ligand on the stroma track, surface/secreted, TCGA-replicated and purity-robust; it already has moderate ccRCC literature, so the analysis reinforces an existing angiogenic-niche hypothesis, and what is missing is normal-tissue (heart) staining and a dependency or perturbation study. The best discovery genes here sit in the stroma and immune tracks (JAG2, GAL3ST4, LILRB4), not in the tumour-cell track.

omics.text: SCARB1 ranks first in the target profile: tumour-up and protein-confirmed [gene=SCARB1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=1.837], purity-robust and TCGA-replicated. However, it is enriched in a vital organ (adrenal) in the GTEx proteome [gene=SCARB1; type=normal_proteome; source=DATASET:GTEX-PROTEOME; vital_protein_ts_max=5.08], a safety concern, and it has no drugs and no selective dependency.

NNMT is up at protein level [gene=NNMT; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.709], tumour-intrinsic and TCGA-replicated. Higher expression predicts worse survival [gene=NNMT; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.301], making it a prognostic biomarker; as an intracellular enzyme it would need a small-molecule rather than antibody strategy.

Negative result: FCER1G is up in bulk tumour but tracks immune infiltration. Its RNA correlates negatively with purity [gene=FCER1G; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_purity_rho=-0.692] and the change shrinks in a pure tumour [gene=FCER1G; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=1.061]. It is an immune-cell signal, not a tumour-cell target.

UMOD shows loss of normal tubule identity, with a massive RNA drop [gene=UMOD; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=-10.31], replicated in TCGA. PSAT1 is down at protein level [gene=PSAT1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=-1.963]. These are diagnostic or prognostic tissue biomarkers, not targets.

SLC16A3 (MCT4, lactate exporter) is up in RNA [gene=SLC16A3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=3.435], with protein support, a cis copy-number effect and purity robustness, but no selective dependency in ccRCC lines. VHL is the mechanism anchor: 3p loss is frequent [gene=VHL; type=omics_cnv; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-CNV; arm=3p; loss_freq=0.791].

literature.text: A single study reports CA9 is preferentially enriched in ccRCC tumour cells with low background in normal kidney, and CA9-targeted PET is proof-of-concept for noninvasive discrimination, warranting prospective validation. High CA9-PET uptake was associated with PBRM1 loss-of-function, immune suppression and angiogenic activity. Omics and the girentuximab programme agree, but the profile shows no prognostic signal and no dependency, so CA9 is a diagnostic/imaging/antibody-delivery target.

CD70 is commonly overexpressed in RCC and minimally expressed in normal tissue; its expression correlates with hypoxia pathway proteins, and two CD70-specific single-domain antibodies were radiolabelled as tracers. The evidence is preclinical or early translational, and the data show no TCGA prognostic significance and no DepMap dependency.

The literature on MT1G contradicts itself on the direction of effect: it is down in ccRCC versus normal kidney yet proposed as a poor-prognosis biomarker, and elevated MT1G promoted growth and metastasis in vitro and in vivo, whereas SAP30-mediated inhibition points to a tumour-suppressive role. MT1G is a biomarker with unresolved biology and not a clear target.
SCARB1 has strong omics and Open Targets genetic association but the corpus has no gene-specific literature relations for it, so it is a data-supported candidate with a literature gap.

external.text: CA9 is a membrane protein (UniProt Q16790) with antibody, small-molecule and PROTAC tractability. Drugs returned: girentuximab (phase 3), iodine-124 girentuximab (phase 2), sulthiame (phase 4) and ethoxzolamide (withdrawn). Negative: DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency and there is no somatic driver mutation.

CD70 is a plasma-membrane ligand of CD27 (UniProt P32970) with antibody tractability. Drugs returned: cusatuzumab (phase 2), vorsetuzumab mafodotin (phase 1) and MDX-1411 (phase 1). It is not a DepMap dependency, so the case rests on surface expression for antibody, ADC or cell therapy; its Open Targets association is low.

NNMT has no drug in Open Targets and no ccRCC dependency, so it is a prognostic biomarker and not a validated vulnerability. COXFA4L2 has only indirect mitochondrial-complex agents (ME-344, metformin) and no selective dependency: a biomarker with a weak target case.

SCARB1 (lipoprotein receptor) combines genetic association with tumour-intrinsic expression and is predicted tractable but has no drug. ALDOB, SLC22A8 and PIGR are down in tumour and are tissue-of-origin loss biomarkers; probenecid and pratosartan listed for SLC22A8 act on a lost gene and are not a rationale. MTOR is an established ccRCC drug target that the expression-led ranking does not capture.

cells.text: Against normal proximal tubule (the cell of origin), paired by donor, CA9 in tumour cells is far higher, log2FC 7.739 [gene=CA9; type=sc_tumor_vs_pt; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; log2fc=7.739], so the signal is tumour-cell specific and not stromal. The attribution holds in the second single-cell dataset.

SCARB1's single-cell attribution does not hold across datasets: the dominant group is myeloid in the first dataset and tumour in the second, with tumour-cell shares of [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.336] and [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.582]. Part of the bulk signal may come from myeloid cells.

NNMT is attributed to tumour cells in both single-cell datasets, with tumour-versus-proximal-tubule log2 fold change [gene=NNMT; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_vs_tubule_log2fc=9.132] in the first and [gene=NNMT; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_vs_tubule_log2fc=5.573] in the second (only a few paired donors).

FCGR3A, high in both rankings, is a microenvironment signal: immune cells make [gene=FCGR3A; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.999] of its tumour transcripts, the tumour-cell share in the first single-cell dataset is [gene=FCGR3A; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.000837], and myeloid cells dominate in both datasets.

discovery.text: RAB42 is the leading tumour-track candidate: it is made mostly by RCC cells, replicates in TCGA and is purity-robust, with very few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug. It is an internal, non-surface protein, so not antibody-accessible, and it has no selective dependency and no survival signal; it remains a weak hypothesis until functional evidence appears.

JAG2 is an endothelial stroma-track Notch ligand, surface or secreted, replicated in TCGA and purity-robust. It has no clinical drug in the screen but moderate ccRCC literature and no selective dependency, so the analysis reinforces an existing angiogenic-niche hypothesis; its safety in heart muscle and other tissues is unresolved.

GAL3ST4 is a macrophage-made immune-track enzyme, replicated in TCGA, purity-robust and linked to adverse survival, with very few ccRCC papers. It is an internal enzyme with no dependency data, so at present it is only a prognostic or myeloid-state marker hypothesis.

LILRB4 is a macrophage surface checkpoint-like receptor. Its tumour-up signal is infiltration-driven (it vanishes in a pure tumour) and replicates in TCGA, with moderate ccRCC literature: a microenvironment immunotherapy hypothesis, not a tumour-cell target. All of these are data-ranked hypotheses and none has a selective dependency.

validation.text: The independent layers strengthen CA9, NNMT, SLC16A3, PSAT1, PCK1 and ALDH6A1, whose protein calls replicate in the confirmatory cohort (SCARB1 also replicates). SLC16A3 protein increase replicates [gene=SLC16A3; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=3.551] and so does NNMT [gene=NNMT; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=4.776]. Fold changes are not comparable in size across technologies.

HK2 protein increase does not replicate: in the confirmatory cohort the log2 fold change is [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-0.256] with adjusted p-value [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=0.074], despite a strong discovery change. Its target rank rests on RNA and discovery protein only.

PPP1R1A protein loss does not replicate: the confirmatory adjusted p-value is [gene=PPP1R1A; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=0.17], although the direction is the same and few matched pairs were available. CA9, CD70, FABP6 and DUSP9 were not tested there (too few matched pairs), which is missing data, not a failed replication. On dependency, only EPAS1 shows a selective effect (borderline), and 2D cell lines miss HIF-2 biology; PRISM drug response and STRING were not run.

PBRM1 is the main genetic driver, mutated recurrently in the cohort, and VHL is also significantly recurrently mutated; CA9 has no somatic driver mutation. Purity extrapolation weakens FCER1G and other immune-cell genes but not CA9, CD70 or SCARB1.

robustness.text: Under random re-weighting of the convergence streams, CA9 and COXFA4L2 are the only genes with robust top-10 membership; ALDOB, CD70, SLC22A8 and SCARB1 are frequently in the top 10 but have wider rank intervals, and PIGR, NNMT, UMOD and FABP1 depend more on the chosen weights. SCARB1 and PIGR fall out of the top 25 without the genetics stream and NNMT without the literature stream, so their position depends on those streams.

treatment.text: CA9 expression is associated with, but does not separate, outcomes between atezolizumab plus bevacizumab and sunitinib in IMmotion150 (difference adjusted p-value [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_between_arms.padj=0.917]); in the sunitinib arm the log hazard ratio per SD is [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.sunitinib.log_hr_per_sd=-0.336], not significant. The nivolumab versus everolimus difference in the second trial is also not significant.

PCK1 is not associated with a differential benefit between atezolizumab plus bevacizumab and sunitinib (difference adjusted p-value [gene=PCK1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_between_arms.padj=0.769]) and has no arm-specific signal, so it is a diagnostic or prognostic lead only. No gene separates the arms of either trial; all treatment statements are associations.

EPAS1 (HIF-2 alpha) is not associated with differential benefit between nivolumab and everolimus (adjusted p-value [gene=EPAS1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_nivolumab_vs_everolimus.padj=0.999]); no IMmotion150 arms were returned for it, so nothing can be said about the atezolizumab combination.

SLC16A3 is not associated with differential benefit between nivolumab and everolimus (adjusted p-value [gene=SLC16A3; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_nivolumab_vs_everolimus.padj=0.999]); higher expression is associated with earlier progression in the nivolumab arm but without significance.

subtypes.text: CA9 is a PBRM1 subgroup target candidate (higher in mutants in CPTAC RNA and TCGA; TCGA RNA mutant minus wild-type log2 difference [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.148]), but the CPTAC protein difference is only borderline and it is lower in ccB than ccA. Mutant-versus-wild-type RNA differences may partly reflect infiltration.
NNMT is not a subgroup candidate: mutant-versus-wild-type differences for VHL, PBRM1, BAP1 and SETD2 and the ccB minus ccA difference are not significant, so it is relevant across genetic subgroups.

PSAT1 differs by molecular subtype: the CPTAC protein ccB minus ccA difference is [gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.cptac_protein.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=0.541], higher in ccB, and BAP1 mutants have higher RNA but not protein, so it is not flagged as a subgroup target.

adc.text: CA9 is a surface protein and a known target (control), but the GTEx proteome flags it as enriched in a vital organ (stomach, tissue-specificity score [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_protein_ts_max=5.19]) with high stomach staining; in the weakest quarter of donors only [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=24.3%] of tumour cells express it. This is a safety and heterogeneity caveat, not proof that a conjugate fails.

CD70 is a surface protein with no vital-organ proteome enrichment (maximum tissue-specificity score [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_protein_ts_max=0.34]), but immunohistochemistry staining data were unavailable and only [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=17.7%] of tumour cells express it in the weakest quarter of donors. Proteome absence is not proof of absence in normal tissue. ENPP3 stains highly in kidney and SLC16A3 is the most uniform but is a multi-pass transporter.

immune.text: CD70 has a large immune-cell component: immune cells make a share of its tumour transcripts of [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.654], and it correlates positively with CD8 T cells; its log hazard ratio on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab is [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; log_hr_atezolizumab_bevacizumab=-0.383]. Tumour-cell expression cannot be separated from immune expression in bulk data, and it was not tested in the confirmatory protein cohort.

integration.text: Omics, literature and external knowledge converge on CA9 and CD70 as surface antigens and on NNMT as a prognostic marker. They disagree where a ranking looks like a target but the layers do not support it: SCARB1 (vital-organ signal, unstable cell attribution), CD70 (immune share), HK2 and PPP1R1A (no confirmatory replication) and the immune genes FCER1G and FCGR3A. Targets: CA9, CD70, SLC16A3, SCARB1 (hypothesis). Biomarkers: NNMT, PSAT1, PCK1, ALDH6A1, UMOD, ALDOB, SLC22A8. Mechanism: VHL, PBRM1, EPAS1, MTOR.

targets.rationale: Top convergence rank, robust to re-weighting, tumour-cell specific and with antibody history (girentuximab); limited by vital-organ (stomach) signal, heterogeneity and no dependency.
Antibody/ADC programmes and tumour-up protein; ranked below CA9 because a large immune-cell share of transcripts and no confirmatory-cohort data blur tumour-cell expression.
Top of the target profile and protein replicated, but placed below CA9/CD70 for the adrenal vital-organ signal and unstable cell-type attribution across single-cell datasets.
Warburg-metabolism membrane transporter with replicated protein increase and purity robustness; no selective dependency and no treatment-arm signal.
Tumour-up membrane enzyme with protein support, TCGA replication and a phase 2 ADC; staining in kidney limits ADC suitability.
Best-supported prognostic biomarker (tumour-intrinsic in both single-cell datasets, protein replicated); an intracellular enzyme with no drug and no dependency, so the target case is weak.
Robust top-10 gene, strongly tumour-up and tumour-intrinsic, but only indirect mitochondrial agents and no dependency.
Top biomarker-profile gene; protein loss replicates and higher expression is linked to worse survival; down-regulated, so not a target.
Strongly down with prognostic association; reflects loss of proximal-tubule identity and may partly reflect tissue composition.
Strongly down with prognostic association in TCGA and literature; tubule-identity marker, not a therapeutic rationale.
Established target (belzutifan) and the only candidate with a selective, borderline DepMap dependency; not captured by the expression-led ranking and no treatment-arm separation.
Established ccRCC drug target (everolimus/temsirolimus) that the expression-led ranking misses; not re-profiled here for dependency.
Exploratory: tumour-cell-made, TCGA-replicated, purity-robust and little studied, but an internal protein with no dependency, survival signal or drug.
Exploratory: endothelial stroma-track Notch ligand, surface/secreted and TCGA-replicated; belongs to the stroma, has existing literature, no dependency and unresolved normal-tissue safety.

limitations.text: The specialists' spatial and structure findings were dropped by verification, so the report has no in-situ or pocket analysis; structural-context scores, where used, are descriptive monomer heuristics and not evidence of a degron or degrader.
COL23A1, OLFML2A and MILR1 were discovery findings from the cells agent that did not pass verification and are not reported; CD74, CXCR4 and KDR microenvironment calls were likewise dropped.
VWF, SLPI, L1CAM, SLC6A19, CYP2J2 and UMOD-adjacent genes (FABP1, NPHS2) replicated or ranked highly but lack separate findings; PNCK and TNFAIP6 had no ADC, immune or trial checks.

Evidence is bulk CPTAC (110 tumours) plus TCGA replication; no candidate has a selective ccRCC dependency except EPAS1 (borderline), and 2D cell lines miss HIF-2 biology. Literature support is single-study and retrospective. Passing automatic checks is not complete scientific validation.
PRISM drug response and STRING were not run, and ranking intervals are heuristic.
